parsed.explanation: The combined regime is split. The state/province is low-risk locally: anti-discrimination, hate-crime, care mandates, public-accommodation protections and no documented facility ban reduce everyday exposure for an outed adult or minor. But the national framework operates at border, visa, airline documents, federal facilities, federal custody and official youth-care hostility. Those cannot be cancelled by local equality law. An outed visitor can face secondary screening, refusal, stranding, fraud/ineligibility, or federal custody; immigration custody has documented beatings, solitary and sexual abuse. No evidence of execution or highly likely imprisonment moves the score into Elevated rather than high/severe.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal rules use M/F only for new documents and visa screening can refuse on sex-marker or presentation discrepancy; fraud/ineligibility possible if wilful misrepresentation suspected. Travelers report blocked/confiscated passports, stranding, and foreign advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiry; limited waivers; court suit and legal FAQ. State marker laws are resident climate, not relief for home documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Airline and border checks precede state protections; state laws cannot pre-empt federal screening.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: If border/fraud triggers custody, federal immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections policies remove HRT and impose conversion-style treatment.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State custody protections and national hate-crime law exist; July assessment still rates state short on inmate protections.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Federal immigration/federal custody can operate around state protections; local custody effect uncertain for visitors.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Federal facility order bars congruent use of government-funded single-sex spaces. State map entry is not provided, so local ban unknown; federal facilities may still restrict access.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public-accommodation nondiscrimination and equal-protection clause likely protect visitors in state/local settings; no criminal bathroom ban documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State law does not cover federal buildings or TSA/airport facilities; exposure depends on actor.

care_services.exposure: National youth-care hostility, school investigations, funding threats, hospital record subpoenas and proposed insurance limits can expose minors and care seekers; state healthcare-equity gap unquantified.
care_services.protection: State mandates insurer/public-program gender-affirming care and bans discrimination; may help adult visitors privately.
care_services.interaction: State care protections may conflict with federal data/insurance actions; visitor eligibility not documented.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders erase gender language, target schools/teachers, and counterterrorism language prioritizes radical pro-transgender groups; could support fraud or security referrals.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime penalties, reporting hotline and constitutional equal protection make local policing protective.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Local police may act protectively, but federal agents may act hostilely.

minors_guardians.exposure: A trans minor or guardian may face document mismatch, border questioning, youth-care scrutiny and records exposure; national rhetoric can frame social transition as deception or fraud.
minors_guardians.protection: State bans conversion therapy on minors, covers care, protects schools against bullying; guardian state legal recognition is climate only.
minors_guardians.interaction: Care/school exposure depends on whether minor uses services; federal policies may still affect records.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No trans-specific violence incident reported for this state/province; absence is not safety, but hostile national climate is a background cue.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State non-discrimination/hate-crime law and hotline; national hate-crime statute provides recourse.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: If violence triggers local police, response likely protective; if federal or airport context, unknown.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Unresolved federal litigation, changing passport rules, officer discretion, missing facilities-map status, unquantified health/custody gaps create uncertainty.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Civil-liberties suit, legal FAQ, state courts, hate-crime hotline, partial injunctions.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are stronger locally than at border/federal custody.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar to Vellandra's border exclusion at first pass: visa/document refusal and stranding possible. But here state public-accommodation protections and existing passport validity reduce everyday risk; federal immigration custody adds severity, keeping it near 0.35-0.45.

Compared to Kestrel Isles secondary screening: border humiliation, delays, possible refusal are comparable, but this dossier documents federal custody abuse and fraud/ineligibility more severely, so score is modestly below 0.55.

Meridia/Cordera border-trained entry is safer than this: matching passport marker and respectful inspection are missing; federal facility/custody hostility remains. State protections only partially offset, so score sits clearly below 0.75.

parsed.synthesis: Practically, adult alone: local day-to-day risk low, but border is highest: document mismatch can cause refusal/fraud/ineligibility, secondary screening, possible detention; if federal custody, abuse severe. Adult with minor: state youth protections reduce school/care risk inside state, but national youth hostility and records subpoena make care/documents more exposed. Remedies likely work locally, less at federal entry. Score reflects Elevated because protective state cannot erase operative federal entry/custody regime, not High/Severe because no execution/certain imprisonment and local safety strong.
